macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: Wall Street falls as technology sell-off deepens
items.summary: The S&P 500 fell 1.1% and the Nasdaq Composite dropped 2.1%, while the Dow declined 0.3%. Chipmakers including Micron and Intel fell sharply as investors questioned the sustainability and financing of the AI investment boom.

items.title: Fed chair avoids signaling October rate decision
items.summary: Fed Chair Kevin Warsh said price stability remains central but declined to prejudge upcoming interest-rate decisions. The comments came amid persistent inflation concerns and market debate over whether the central bank will raise rates later this year.

items.title: Markets enter a week dominated by inflation, PMI data and megacap earnings
items.summary: Investors are watching preliminary U.S. and European PMI figures, inflation signals and earnings from Meta and Tesla. The Nasdaq fell 4.48% for the week, compared with declines of 1.95% for the S&P 500 and 0.67% for the Dow.

items.title: Fed blackout begins ahead of October policy meeting
items.summary: The Federal Reserve entered its communications blackout before the October 27–28 meeting, limiting official guidance as markets reassess rate expectations. Roughly 70 S&P 500 companies, including Tesla, Meta, Western Digital and AT&T, are scheduled to report earnings next week.

items.title: JPMorgan profit misses estimates as Dimon flags economic uncertainty
items.summary: JPMorgan Chase reported third-quarter profit of $15.3 billion, or $5.57 per share, below analysts’ $5.90 estimate. CEO Jamie Dimon warned about shifting economic forces.

items.title: China plans restrictions on exports of strategic technologies
items.summary: China plans to restrict or prohibit exports of 40 technologies, including artificial intelligence, semiconductor and solar-power technologies, intensifying trade and supply-chain tensions.

items.title: Oil rises as geopolitical risks amplify inflation concerns
items.summary: Brent crude rose 3.7% as escalating tensions involving Iran and the Strait of Hormuz, along with attacks on Russian energy infrastructure, increased concerns about energy supply and inflation.

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin briefly drops below $80,000 before recovering above $82,000
items.summary: Bitcoin briefly fell below $80,000 before rebounding to roughly $82,500. Separate market data showed BTC above $82,000 with gains of about 0.2%–0.8% over 24 hours.[3][4][8]

items.title: Bitcoin short-term holders send more than 50,000 BTC to exchanges
items.summary: Analyst Darkfost reported that short-term holders transferred more than 50,000 BTC to exchanges in 24 hours, including about 29,500 BTC moved at a loss—the largest such realized loss in nearly four months.[1]

items.title: Russia plans to restrict direct peer-to-peer crypto transactions
items.summary: The Bank of Russia said direct individual-to-individual crypto transactions will be allowed only until July 1, 2027, after which authorized intermediaries must process them. It also said transfers from digital accounts to self-custodial wallets are prohibited.[4]

items.title: U.S. stablecoin implementation rule expected by end of October
items.summary: The head of the U.S. Office of the Comptroller of the Currency reportedly said the agency’s final rule implementing the GENIUS Act is expected no later than the end of October.[4]

items.title: UK sanctions crypto firms linked to Russia-related sanctions evasion
items.summary: The United Kingdom imposed sanctions on Cryptomus, Heleket and TokenSpot, alleging links to Russia-related sanctions evasion. TokenSpot reportedly transferred more than $950 million to sanctioned exchanges and networks.[1]

items.title: Polygon releases Bor update fixing denial-of-service vulnerabilities
items.summary: Polygon Labs released Bor v2.10.3 to address two medium-severity denial-of-service vulnerabilities affecting BlockSTM V2 parallel block execution.[4]

items.title: More than $900 million in crypto positions liquidated
items.summary: Nearly $934 million in crypto positions were liquidated across about 167,400 trader accounts, with Bitcoin and Ethereum recording the heaviest losses amid market volatility.[7]

items.title: U.S. government-linked wallet transfers 12,267 BTC
items.summary: An address labeled as holding seized Bitfinex-hack funds transferred 12,267 BTC, valued at approximately $1.01 billion.[1]

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: Google releases Gemini 4 Argon
items.summary: Google has made Gemini 4 Argon available to developers and enterprises through the Gemini API, while also rolling it out to select consumer products. The company positions it for complex multi-step work in coding, finance, legal, cybersecurity and science, though reported benchmark results are vendor claims.

items.title: DeepSeek releases V4.1-Flash-1017
items.summary: DeepSeek released an updated V4.1 Flash model that it says improves reasoning, coding, agentic and vision performance while reducing token usage and task time. The release also includes a search API, according to industry coverage.

items.title: Anthropic announces Claude Sonnet 5.5
items.summary: Anthropic announced Claude Sonnet 5.5, claiming more than 30% faster generation and up to 30% lower cost per task than its predecessor while keeping the same list price. The model is also reported to power Claude’s free tier.

items.title: OpenAI reportedly releases new GPT-6 variants
items.summary: Industry reports describe OpenAI launches including GPT-6 Astra Ultrafast and GPT-6.1 Sol, with the latter emphasizing lower-cost agentic coding, computer use and professional-work workloads. The reported releases and specifications were not corroborated by a primary OpenAI source in the available results.

items.title: Meta introduces Muse Spark Open
items.summary: Meta announced Muse Spark Open, an open-weight model designed for local execution on high-memory Apple computers. The model reportedly uses sparse activation, with only a fraction of its total parameters active for each token.

items.title: CERN and Mistral plan physics foundation model
items.summary: CERN and Mistral signed a statement of intent to develop a large physics model trained on simulated Large Hadron Collider data. The proposed system would support particle reconstruction and identification for collider research.

items.title: China considers expanded AI export controls
items.summary: China’s commerce and science ministries reportedly proposed adding 23 AI-related technologies—including large models, agents, chip designs and computing clusters—to the country’s export-control list. The proposal indicates continued tightening around strategic AI capabilities.

items.title: Weizmann researchers develop Brain-IT
items.summary: Researchers at the Weizmann Institute of Science developed Brain-IT, an AI system that reconstructs images a person is viewing or imagining from high-resolution fMRI data. The result highlights ongoing progress in neural decoding and brain–computer interfaces.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: Xbox announces Xbox Labs for browser-based gaming
items.summary: Microsoft has created Xbox Labs, a small engineering unit exploring ways to make older-generation games playable in web browsers and distribute or create games across more devices.

items.title: Epic reportedly delays Disney-related Marvel and Star Wars shooter
items.summary: Epic Games has reportedly delayed its unannounced Disney project indefinitely while directing developers toward fully AI-generated art and AI-focused development workflows.

items.title: Indie game demo canceled over AI copying concerns
items.summary: The developers of Drunken Goddess Reflux canceled a planned public demo, citing concerns that its gameplay and presentation could be rapidly copied with AI tools before launch. Closed demonstrations will replace the public event.

items.title: Hillthorn receives November release date
items.summary: The card-based detective game Hillthorn is scheduled to launch on November 10 for Nintendo Switch, PC, and mobile devices, alongside a new gameplay trailer.

items.title: The Wolf Among Us Remastered Switch version delayed
items.summary: Telltale has postponed the Nintendo Switch release of The Wolf Among Us Remastered indefinitely, saying the team needs more time to meet its quality goals.

items.title: Esports updates span Counter-Strike 2, StarCraft, Rainbow Six Siege, and Marvel Rivals
items.summary: Recent tournament results included an upset in the PGL Bucharest qualifier, while StarCraft’s ASL reached its 22nd season. New fan and data tools, including a Sheep Esports mobile app, also launched.

tech_news.query: What are the most important technology news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major product launches, company news, and significant tech industry developments. Exclude AI-specific news.

items.title: GlobalFoundries plans two New York chip plants
items.summary: GlobalFoundries is set to open two semiconductor plants in New York, backed by $21 billion in financing from Japan. The expansion would increase U.S. chip-manufacturing capacity.

items.title: Florida wins ruling on social-media law for children
items.summary: A court ruling allows Florida to enforce a law restricting children’s use of social-media platforms. The decision could influence similar regulations and ongoing legal battles across the United States.

items.title: Analogue announces updated retro gaming consoles
items.summary: Analogue announced the Super Nt Plus and Mega Sg Plus, updated versions of its retro gaming consoles designed to play classic Super Nintendo and Sega Genesis games on modern displays.

items.title: Google rolls out Universal Cart in the United States
items.summary: Google has launched Universal Cart across Google Search and the Gemini app, allowing shoppers to combine products from multiple retailers into one cart.

items.title: Apple updates App Store rules for intimate-image apps
items.summary: Apple has explicitly prohibited applications that create non-consensual intimate images, including so-called nudify apps, under updated App Store guidelines.

items.title: Oxide raises $445 million in Series D funding
items.summary: Rack-scale cloud-computer maker Oxide announced a $445 million Series D round led by Eclipse, with participation from existing investors and AMD as a strategic investor.
